title: Napoleon besieges Acre; Bashir II stays neutral
why: Jazzar accused Bashir of supplying the French; the rift led to his 1799 flight from Mount Lebanon. Siege lasted about two months.

title: Bashir II ousted from Deir al-Qamar by Jazzar
why: Jazzar sent a force to help Jirji Baz remove Bashir, who fled north to Akkar with Sheikh Bashir Jumblatt (date given as 1799).

title: Grand Vizier grants Bashir II fiscal authority over Lebanon
why: After Sidney Smith's mediation at al-Arish, Bashir got tax authority over Mount Lebanon, Wadi al-Taym, Bekaa and Jabal Amil, though he lacked real control.

title: Bashir II and Jirji Baz agree to share Mount Lebanon
why: Bashir kept Druze areas and Keserwan; Yusuf's sons the north (Jubail, Batroun). Oath sworn on Quran and Gospel; Baz became his mudabbir. Jazzar was angered.

title: Most Druze sheikhs rally to Bashir II, condemn Imad clan
why: After four years of Yazbaki-backed rival Shihab claimants failing, the Druze sheikhs backed Bashir in 1803.

title: Jazzar Pasha dies; Sulayman Pasha later governs Sidon
why: Jazzar died April-May 1804. Isma'il seized Acre against the Porte; Sulayman, his mamluk, was named wali of Sidon in 1805.

title: Sulayman Pasha al-Adil appointed wali of Sidon
why: He ruled from Acre to 1819 by decentralisation and diplomacy with local sheikhs including Emir Bashir; he led the last functioning mamluk system.

title: Sulayman defeats Isma'il, who held Acre
why: His forces beat Isma'il when he sortied from Acre (late 1805 or early 1806), securing Sulayman's control of the Sidon Eyalet.

title: Bashir II has Jirji Baz strangled
why: Bashir's Druze partisans then occupied Jubail, killed Baz's brother and blinded Yusuf's sons, ending the northern rival power.

title: Maronite Patriarch Tiyyan pushed to step down
why: After Baz's killing Bashir pressured Patriarch Yusuf al-Tiyyan to resign, removing a Maronite counterweight.

title: Sulayman Pasha gives Bashir II life lease of Chouf and Keserwan
why: Effectively made Bashir ruler for life; Sulayman addressed him as 'our noble son'. Annual tribute and Jumblatt dominance still limited him.

title: Bashir, Sulayman and Jumblatt mobilise at Tiberias against Wahhabi threat
why: Damascus's wali asked for help; the Wahhabi force withdrew to the Hejaz before the Jordan was crossed.

title: Bashir II vaccinated against smallpox
why: Noted in a footnote as an early vaccination of a Levantine ruler during local smallpox prevalence.

title: Beit ed-Dine becomes seat of the emirate
why: Capital moved from Deir al-Qamar (1600-1811) to Beit ed-Dine (1811-1842); the palace was built by Bashir II.

title: Muhammad Ali massacres Egypt's mamluks; survivors reach Acre
why: A few escaped to Sulayman Pasha, who bought hundreds of mamluks in 1812; Acre became the 'last mamluk stronghold'.

title: Lady Hester Stanhope excavates Ascalon
why: Early use of a textual source by field archaeologists; she later settled near Sidon at Mar Elias, Abra, then Joun.

title: Maronite 'ammiya' peasants meet at Antelias, reject Bashir's taxes
why: Patriarch Yusuf Istifan rallied some 6,000 peasants against a doubled jizya and kharaj; Yazbakis named Hasan and Salman as emirs on 14 April.

title: Bashir II goes into exile in the Hauran
why: Under Dervish Pasha's protection with Sheikh Bashir Jumblatt, after Abdullah Pasha sided with the peasants.

title: Sulayman Pasha dies in Acre
why: Buried beside Jazzar; Abdullah Pasha succeeded him in January 1820.

title: Abdullah Pasha becomes governor of Sidon and demands extra taxes
why: He asked Bashir for a 1 million dirham payment, prompting the advance jizya levy that triggered the ammiya.

title: First American Protestant missionaries reach Beirut area (ABCFM)
why: Pliny Fisk and Levi Parsons began the Levant mission; permanent Beirut station followed in 1823. (Fisk sailed from Boston 3 Nov 1819.)

title: Bashir II regains emirate by agreement with rival emirs
why: Hasan and Salman stood down; a referendum was promised but Abdullah Pasha restored Bashir first, on condition he collect the jizya.

title: Northern Maronites and Shia rise against Bashir at Lehfed, Haqil, Ehmej
why: Wukala demanded fiscal equality with the Druze; Bashir crushed them with Abu Nakad Druze fighters, widening the Maronite-Druze gap.

title: Bashir takes the Beqaa for Abdullah Pasha, clashes with Damascus
why: Son Khalil conquered the Beqaa from Dervish Pasha's deputy; the Porte sent Aleppo's Mustafa Pasha against Abdullah and Bashir.

title: Porte replaces Bashir with Abbas As'ad Shihab
why: Sheikh Bashir Jumblatt defected to the governors; Acre was besieged. (Other sources may differ by days.)

title: Bashir II sails to Egypt in exile
why: Lost Jumblatt backing; found a powerful ally in Muhammad Ali, who secured pardons and the lifting of the Acre siege in March 1822.

title: Siege of Acre lifted after Muhammad Ali's pardon
why: Pardons for Bashir and Abdullah Pasha; Bashir promised 4,000 fighters to Muhammad Ali in return.

title: Aleppo-Antioch earthquake, felt along the Lebanese coast
why: M~7.0 on the Dead Sea Transform; 20,000 deaths regarded as likely (range 30,000-60,000 reported). One source reports a tsunami hitting Lebanon's coast; Ambraseys found none.

title: Isaac Bird and William Goodell found the first permanent American mission station in Beirut
why: Station HQ became known as 'Burj Bird'. They sailed late 1822 via Malta.

title: Mission wives open a school for Arab children in Beirut
why: Mrs Bird and Mrs Goodell started it; by 1825 Bird's school had 85 Syrian pupils.

title: Bashir's forces lose to Sheikh Bashir Jumblatt's
why: A setback before Abdullah Pasha's 500 Albanian irregulars arrived on 2 January 1825.

title: Bashir II routs Jumblatt near Moukhtara
why: With Albanian reinforcements from Abdullah Pasha; Sheikh Bashir and Ali Imad fled to the Hauran.

title: Sheikh Bashir Jumblatt executed at Acre
why: Abdullah Pasha acted at Muhammad Ali's request; Ali Imad was executed by Damascus forces. Jumblatt and Imad homes were then destroyed.

title: Bashir centralises: Sharia-based code, three appointed qadis
why: Jurisdiction moved from Druze muqata'jis to qadis at Deir al-Qamar, Ghazir/Zouk Mikael and Zgharta; custom still applied in practice.

title: Jumblatt tax districts redistributed to Shihab, Talhuq and Abu Nakad
why: Chouf, Kharrub, Tuffah, Jezzine and Bekaa lost to Jumblatts and given to Khalil Shihab and allies; many Druze left for the Hauran.

title: Pliny Fisk dies in Beirut
why: The missionary and Arabic linguist died of fever; on his last day he completed an English and Arabic dictionary.

title: Greek flotilla raids Beirut, briefly holds a seafront quarter
why: About fifteen ships under Vasos Mavrovouniotis; a mufti-led defence repelled them. Abdullah Pasha sent ~500 Albanians on 23 March.

title: Asad al-Shidyaq, first Maronite convert to Protestantism, confined by church
why: He sent theological objections to Bishop Karam; held in monasteries from early 1826 and died in 1830.

title: Shams Shihab, Bashir's wife, dies; mausoleum built at Beit ed-Dine
why: Bashir married Hisn Jihan (Circassian, converted to Maronite) in 1833.

title: Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army begins conquest of Syria
why: Muhammad Ali's pretext was complaints against Abdullah Pasha, who sheltered Egyptian draft fugitives. (Another source says Acre siege opened October 1831.)

title: Egyptians besiege Abdullah Pasha in Acre
why: Both sides wooed Bashir II, who hesitated until Egypt threatened to wreck Mount Lebanon's silk economy.

title: Bashir II sides with Muhammad Ali
why: Decided after Jumblatt's sons joined Ibrahim's camp; Druze clans (Abu Nakad, Jumblatt, Talhuq, Imad, Arslan) joined the Ottoman army, which named Nu'man Jumblatt in his place.

title: Acre falls to Ibrahim Pasha
why: After a six-month siege; Bashir's Maronite troops then marched on Damascus. (Other sources: 27 May 1832.)

title: Damascus taken without resistance by Egyptians and Khalil Shihab's troops
why: Bashir's son Khalil commanded Mount Lebanon contingents; Homs followed on 9 July (another source: 8 July).

title: Muhammad Ali extends Bashir's jurisdiction to Jabal Amil, Koura, Sidon and Beirut
why: Egyptian rule abolished the eyalets of Damascus, Aleppo, Tripoli and Sidon, but Bashir kept direct control of Mount Lebanon; Beirut became silk outlet.

title: Beirut revival begins after Ibrahim captures Acre
why: Beirut had declined to about 10,000 people under Jazzar and Abdullah; Egyptian rule restored it as the Syrian coast's commercial and diplomatic centre.

title: Ibrahim routs Ottoman army at Konya
why: Lebanese troops under Khalil Shihab also fought at Konya (27 Dec in another account). Opened route towards Constantinople.

title: American Press moved to Beirut
why: Isaac Bird's 'Thirteen Letters' replying to the Maronite bishop were printed in Arabic there in 1833.

title: Convention of Kutahya cedes Syria to Muhammad Ali
why: Ibrahim Pasha became governor-general of Syria, including Mount Lebanon, with a more coercive centralised regime.

title: Bashir marries Hisn Jihan
why: Circassian slave girl, converted to the Maronite Church; Bashir built her a palace at Beit ed-Dine. Her influence was reputed.

title: William McClure Thomson arrives in Beirut
why: Later documented the 1837 earthquake in 'The Land and the Book' (1859).

title: Muhammad Ali's centralisation ends tax farming (1833/34)
why: Tax collection moved from muqata'jis to central appointees; Bashir confiscated their estates and installed relatives as mutasallims.

title: Lazarists open Collège Saint Joseph in Antoura with seven pupils
why: Described as the Middle East's oldest French school and first francophone secondary school; Antoura mission dated from 1773.

title: Peasants' revolt against Egyptian conscription spreads from Palestine
why: Bashir led troops against Safed; rebels surrendered at Bint Jbeil and Druze under Amin Shihab entered Safed on 18 July.

title: Ibrahim Pasha storms Al-Karak in pursuit of rebel leader Qasim al-Ahmad
why: Seventeen-day siege; the town was destroyed and orchards uprooted.

title: Bashir II's forces, led by Khalil Shihab and relatives, help suppress revolts in Akkar, Safita, Krak and Latakia
why: Khalil Shihab and relatives took part in 1834-35 operations; Mount Lebanon was allowed to keep its arms. (corrected from 1834 and from "Lebanese forces": Wikipedia says Bashir's forces took part between 1834 and 1835)

title: Isaac Bird leaves Syria
why: He left in 1836 after serving at Beirut since 1823.

title: Galilee earthquake damages Beirut, Sidon and Tyre
why: M 6.25-6.5; felt in Baalbek (VI) and Damascus (VII). Beirut shock slight but houses fell; Tyre streets blocked; Safed destroyed.

title: Egyptian-run Syria: Ibrahim's chief of staff Beaufort d'Hautpoul serves 1834-1837
why: French officer assisted Ibrahim Pasha, linking French influence to the Egyptian administration.

title: Druze revolt against Egyptian conscription begins in the Hauran
why: First reports in January; 400 troops under Ali Agha al-Busayli were defeated at Tha'la.

title: Egyptians defeat Druze in Wadi al-Taym
why: 33 Druze and 13 Egyptians killed; Shibli al-Aryan then took Rashaya. Ibrahim ordered Bashir to send men.

title: Bashir II mobilises Christian force against Druze rebels
why: Grandson Mahmud led it; ambushed by rival Shihab emirs; Khalil came to aid. Tensions between Christians and Druze rose.

title: Decisive Druze defeat in Wadi al-Taym; Nasir ad-Din Imad killed
why: About 640 Druze lost; Hasan Jumblatt and Imad had led them. Ibrahim then crushed the rest at Shebaa (17 July).

title: Druze rebels enter Safed, plunder the Jewish quarter for three days
why: Local militia abandoned the city; many residents fled to Acre.

title: Egypt and Druze leaders sign peace ending the revolt
why: Amnesty, labour in lieu of conscription, surrender of arms, mediated by Hasan al-Bitar and Jiris Abu ad-Dibs. Disarmament dragged to August.

title: Ibrahim distributes 16,000 rifles to Mount Lebanon Christians
why: Reward for supporting Egypt in the 1838 revolt; communal fault lines deepened.

title: Egyptians defeat Ottoman army at Nezib
why: Ibrahim Pasha won; Sultan Mahmud II died days later and the Ottoman fleet defected to Muhammad Ali on 1 July.

title: Lady Hester Stanhope dies at Joun
why: British traveller who lived in Lebanon from c.1814, died at an abandoned monastery near Sidon.

title: Anti-Egyptian rebellion launched in Mount Lebanon
why: British-Ottoman backed alliance of Abu Nakad, Abu'l Lama, Khazen, Shihab, Hubaysh and Dahdah clans plus Maronite leaders; largely Matn, Keserwan and the Sahil.

title: Napier's British squadron sent to the Syrian coast
why: Admiral Stopford dispatched Commodore Charles Napier, who acted independently off Beirut.

title: Bashir reports first rebellion suppressed; 57 leaders exiled to Upper Egypt
why: Haydar Abu'l Lama and Fransis al-Khazen among them; rebel arms redistributed to Sa'd al-Din of Hasbaya.

title: Convention of London for the Pacification of the Levant signed
why: UK, Austria, Prussia and Russia offered Muhammad Ali hereditary Egypt; ten days to accept withdrawal or lose southern Syria, 20 days or forfeit all.

title: Napier's ships appear off Beirut, demand Egyptians leave
why: He called on Sulayman Pasha to abandon the town; population revolt followed, but 15,000 Egyptian troops limited his options until September.

title: Consul Wood's three offers to Bashir II to defect, all refused
why: Wood had won Patriarch Hubaysh with guarantees on Maronite privileges; Bashir still sided with Muhammad Ali.

title: Allied bombardment of Beirut begins; landing at Jounieh
why: British and Austrian ships bombarded; ~1,500 Turks and marines landed at Jounieh. (Other sources: Sidon shelled the same day.)

title: Allies arm Bashir Qasim Shihab's rebels from Jounieh base
why: Bashir Qasim attacked Egyptians in Beirut, Sidon and Acre; Ibrahim Pasha moved to Mount Lebanon from northern Syria.

title: Allied squadron bombards Sidon; city capitulates within two days
why: Napier led the storming column; earlier a sortie won at Nahr el-Kelb.

title: Egyptians abandon Beirut
why: Per one account; another says allies held Beirut, Sidon, Haifa and Tyre by 25 September.

title: Sultan Abdulmecid I deposes Bashir II, names Bashir Qasim
why: Firman issued after Bashir refused to defect.

title: Allies defeat Ibrahim's army at Boharsef
why: Napier disobeyed an order to retire from command to press the attack on the heights; Egypt had already left Beirut.

title: Bashir II surrenders to the Ottomans, sails into exile in Malta
why: He offered 4 million piastres to go to France, refused; took 113 retainers incl. Jihan and Patriarch's Bishop Hubaysh. Later Istanbul (died 1850).

title: Allies bombard Acre; magazine explosion kills about 1,100
why: Ships fired 48,000 rounds; allied losses 18 killed, 41 wounded; the last Egyptian coastal position fell.

title: Muhammad Ali accepts Convention; renounces Syria
why: Hereditary rule of Egypt and Sudan; army capped at 18,000; Ottoman fleet returned. Ended Egyptian rule in Lebanon.

title: Governor of Sidon moves his seat to Beirut
why: Made Beirut effectively the new capital of the Sidon eyalet.

title: Butrus al-Bustani moves to Beirut, works as dragoman for the British
why: Later taught for American missionaries; became a leading Nahda figure.

title: Nasif al-Yaziji moves to Beirut; becomes Arabic tutor to missionaries
why: Later (1847) formed the first Arab literary society with Bustani.

title: Dr Cornelius Van Dyck sent to Lebanon as medical missionary
why: Studied Arabic under al-Bustani and al-Yaziji; later led the 1865 Arabic Bible.

title: Ibrahim Pasha completes evacuation of Syria
why: Harassed along the Hajj road as his army withdrew to Gaza.

title: Ottoman Porte installs Bashir III Shihab as emir
why: Hardly popular; nicknamed 'Abu Taheen'. Druze families besieged him in Deir al-Qamar from October 1841.

title: Porte lets Sulayman annex most of Tripoli Eyalet to Sidon Eyalet
why: Including the Latakia sanjak; Sidon Eyalet already included Gaza sanjak since Jazzar.

title: Bashir orders Shihabs to observe Ramadan publicly
why: Followed Ottoman suppression of the Wahhabi revolt and Jumblatt's open Sunni stance; deeply offended the Maronite Church.

title: Abdullah Pasha formally succeeds Sulayman as wali of Sidon
why: Haim Farhi, who bribed the Porte for the appointment, was strangled and thrown from Acre's walls months later.

title: Faris al-Shidyaq leaves Lebanon for Egypt after brother As'ad's ordeal
why: From 1825 to 1848 he lived between Cairo and Malta, where he ran the American mission press.

title: American Protestant mission established in Hasbaya
why: Reported in an unsourced line on the town's page; treat as tentative.

title: As'ad al-Shidyaq dies after years of confinement
why: First Lebanese Protestant convert; held in Qannoubine and other monasteries after 1826 on the Patriarch's orders.

title: Ottoman firman of 1839 equalises status of Muslim and non-Muslim subjects
why: Tanzimat milestone; Ottoman Syria page links it to growing Muslim-Christian alienation culminating in 1860. Exact day not stated in page read. (day added: 3 November 1839)

title: Napier blockades Alexandria, then negotiates with Muhammad Ali
why: His independent peace was first repudiated by Stopford, but formed the basis of the final treaty confirmed by the Sultan.

title: Druze families besiege Bashir III in Deir al-Qamar palace
why: They arrived armed to talk tax policy; the stalemate ended in January 1842 when the Sultan withdrew his appointment and Bashir III went to Constantinople.

title: Sultan withdraws Bashir III; he goes into exile in Constantinople
why: End of the Shihab emirate. Bashir III had been born 1775; died 1860 (other source).
